_comment: Copy to ~/.config/viewport/config.json, or pass --config PATH.
This is the tier that must keep working when the web shell does not.
The shell is fetched over the network; if it 404s, throws, or hangs,
anything it owned dies with it. Bindings defined here still work in
that state, which is the difference between a broken desktop UI and a
machine you cannot quit without switching to a TTY.
The shell may add more bindings at runtime with bind.add over IPC.
That layer is additive and expendable; keep exit and a terminal here.
Precedence: command-line flags > this file > built-in defaults.
Two ways to write keybindings, and this file demonstrates the heavier
one. Defining any "binds" object at all suppresses the built-in
defaults, so an empty one means 'no keybindings' — that is what it is
for, and it is why everything below has to be spelled out.
To change a few chords and keep the rest, use "binds_override"
instead. It is not shown here because there would be nothing to show:
"binds_override": { "Mod4+Return": "exec foot", "Mod4+d": null }
opens foot instead of the built-in terminal, lets Mod4+d through to the
focused application, and leaves every other default alone. A null (or
the action "none") unbinds a chord, which is not the same as leaving
it out: leaving it out is what asks for the built-in.
_layout: "tiling"   i3/sway: splits, plus tabbed and stacked containers.
"scrolling" niri: an endless strip of columns that scrolls to follow
focus. Opening a window never resizes the ones already
open. Changes the default movement bindings to match:
Mod4+h/l walk the strip, Mod4+j/k move inside a column,
Mod4+comma/period consume and expel, Mod4+r cycles the
column width.
"solar"     the focused window in the middle at 60% of the screen, the
rest in orbit around it — eight at full size in the margin,
the rest at the edges and corners drawn at 40% and dimmed.
Focus is what puts a window in the middle, so the one being
typed into is never shrunk, dimmed or covered. Mod4+h/j/k/l
cast a ray from the middle rather than comparing edges,
Mod4+[ and Mod4+] rotate the orbit, Mod4+= and Mod4+- grow
and shrink the middle one, Mod4+Shift+s throws a window at
the other monitor. See docs/solar.md.
"matrix"    the focused window at 60% of the width on the left, and the
focus history halving away down the right: the one before
this at half the column, the one before that a quarter, and
so on until a slot would be under 100px. What is left over
is stacked in the last slot with a count on it. Order is
Alt+Tab order, so nothing is placed by where it sits in the
tree. No keys of its own — focus is the only input the model
takes. See docs/matrix.md.
"shell layout.model" switches at runtime; with no argument it cycles.
_tiling_mode: How the tiling tree arranges itself. Only meaningful with
"layout": "tiling" — the scrolling strip, the solar layout and the
matrix are each their own model.
"manual"        the tree of splits you make. The default.
"master-stack"  first window one side, the rest in a column beside it.
"spiral"        each window halves what is left, turning each time.
"bsp"           the same, cutting along the region's longer side.
The dynamic modes derive the shape from which windows are open, so
opening one rearranges what is already there — and resize weights reset
when that happens, which is why manual is the default.
"shell layout.mode" switches at runtime; with no argument it cycles.
_focus_crosses_outputs: Whether Mod4+h and Mod4+l — and Mod4+j and Mod4+k — carry focus onto the
next monitor once there is nothing left to reach on this one. True is
sway's behaviour and the default. False stops directional focus at the
edge of the screen, which is worth having on a wide pair of monitors
where the last window on one is a keypress away from focusing something
Asking for a monitor by name is unaffected: a binding on
"shell output.focus right" still crosses. This is about falling off the
end of a screen, not about ever leaving it.
_bar: "visible" always, "hidden" never, or "auto", which reveals the bar
only while Mod4 is held. "auto" is for OLED panels: the bar is the one
part of the screen that never changes, which is what burns in. Mod4+n
still toggles it per output regardless of the mode.
_empty: What the shell draws when a workspace has no windows: the mark, and the
note naming the keys that open something. Worth having the first time
and steadily less so after that. With both off the desktop is empty,
which on an OLED panel is one fewer thing sitting in fixed pixels.
_theme: Colours for the shell, set as CSS custom properties. Any name the
stylesheet reads works; the ones it defines are bg, text, muted, border,
border-focus, bar-bg, bar-border, glow-1, glow-2, bar, radius, tab and
gap. Values are colours or lengths,
not arbitrary CSS. On an OLED panel a true black bg costs no light at
all, which is the only background that does.
_outputs: Modes are left to the display by default. max_refresh takes the fastest
refresh rate available at the preferred resolution, which is what a
high-refresh monitor that nominates a 60Hz timing needs. A named mode
may leave the refresh off to match on resolution alone. An exact name
beats "*" whichever order they appear in.
_adaptive_sync: Variable refresh rate. Off by default because it depends on the monitor
and the driver as much as on the compositor, and enabling it where it is
not properly supported causes flicker. Tested against the hardware at
startup and quietly left off if it is refused.
_idle: What to do when nobody is there. Both thresholds are in seconds and
either can be omitted; with neither set there is no policy at all and an
external daemon such as swayidle can own it instead.
The compositor does not draw the lock screen itself — it runs the locker
named here, so that the program drawing it can crash without unlocking
anything. Checked every 5 seconds, so thresholds round up to that.
